description: Test your knowledge of the anterior abdominal wall anatomy, including planes, regions, muscles, and fascia.

cards.text: What are the main structures found in the right upper quadrant (RUQ)?
cards.answer: Liver (right lobe), gallbladder, right kidney, and hepatic flexure of the colon.

tip.tip: Remember: **Liver, Gallbladder, right Kidney, Hepatic flexure** — the hepatobiliary organs are here.

cards.text: Which plane passes through the pylorus, pancreatic neck, origin of the superior mesenteric artery, and the hilum of both kidneys?
cards.answer: The transpyloric plane (L1), located midway between the suprasternal notch and pubic symphysis.

tip.tip: L1 = the **most clinically packed single plane** in the abdomen — remember it for clinical exams.

cards.text: In which direction do external oblique muscle fibers run, and what is the mnemonic for remembering this?
cards.answer: Downward and medially, like **hands in pockets**. Bilaterally compresses the abdomen; unilaterally causes ipsilateral flexion and contralateral rotation.

tip.tip: **Hands in pockets = downward and medial** — the most intuitive anatomical mnemonic.

cards.text: What are the tendinous intersections of the rectus abdominis, and why do sit-ups create a 'six-pack'?
cards.answer: 3–4 fibrous bands that interrupt the muscle belly, attaching only to the anterior rectus sheath. Sit-ups create segmentation because contractions bulge between these fixed attachment points.

tip.tip: Tendinous intersections = **anterior sheath only** — this asymmetry is why the six-pack is visible.

cards.text: What is the primary action of the transversus abdominis muscle?
cards.answer: Pure abdominal compression. It is the main muscle activated during Valsalva maneuvers (cough, sneeze, defecation, micturition, childbirth).

tip.tip: **Transverse fibers = squeeze like a corset** — the deepest compressor of the abdomen.

cards.text: From superficial to deep, what is the anatomical order of the three flat (lateral) muscles of the anterolateral abdomen?
cards.answer: External oblique → Internal oblique → Transversus abdominis (EIT).

tip.tip: **EIT (Eight-Teen)** — like a countdown: 8 = external, internal is next, transverse last.

cards.text: What is the difference in unilateral actions between the external oblique and internal oblique muscles?
cards.answer: External oblique (unilateral) → contralateral rotation + ipsilateral flexion. Internal oblique (unilateral) → ipsilateral rotation (opposite rotational direction).

tip.tip: External and internal fibers are **perpendicular** — their rotations go opposite directions when activated alone.

cards.text: What are the three key horizontal planes that divide the abdomen into nine regions, and what vertebral levels do they correspond to?
cards.answer: Transpyloric plane (L1), subcostal plane (L3), and intertubercular plane (L5). These create the 3×3 grid with epigastrium, umbilical, and hypogastric regions.

tip.tip: **L1-L3-L5** — remember the odd numbers: 1, 3, 5 = top, middle, bottom.
